model: Owner-FCF DCF on Company excluding Ford Credit, sum-of-parts with Ford Credit at book equity in the bridge (engine route)

inputs.sbc_source: Consolidated cash-flow statement 'Stock compensation': FY2025 $510M (F_Annual_FY2025.txt:7751), 9M-2026 $324M (F_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:3052) annualised to ~$430M. Ford publishes no separate net-share-settlement tax line and no combined equity-award figure, so sbc_incl_equity_taxes = the cash-flow add-back; the omission is small (<0.1% of revenue).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T21:02:01Z regular close (Friday); valuation dated Sunday 2026-11-08, no after-hours print involved
inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares, Q3 2026 10-Q EPS table (F_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:3339): 4,076M, versus 3,979M basic at FY2025. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice. Ford buys back only to offset SBC dilution ($311M in 9M-2026, $0 in FY2025), so the flat count is roughly funded in practice.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. 10y UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.4 gives a cost of equity ~11%; the automotive business is net cash on an unrestricted-cash basis but carries $23.7B of gross debt at ~5.5% pre-tax (BBB-/Ba1), so a market-weight WACC lands ~9%. 9.5% is used, identical across all three scenarios: cyclicality, tariff and Model e risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate (adaptations rule f). Terminal growth 2.0% base / 1.5% bear / 2.5% bull; terminal cap 12x owner FCF base/bull, 10x bear -- a cyclical OEM has never commanded a mature-compounder multiple.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt, but immaterial: Ford's operating-lease liabilities (~$2.4B total, F_Annual_FY2025.txt:9672) are not in AutomotiveDebt and not deducted here; lease expense stays inside EBIT (US GAAP ASC 842 operating leases are expensed in EBIT, so no principal/interest split is needed). Finance lease payments (~$0.1B/yr) are inside the debt figure. Effect on value < $0.60/share either way.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interests are negligible ($8M of 9M-2026 net income, $37M of equity); flows are treated as fully attributable and no NCI deduction is made in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE. Ford straddles two routing rows: a cyclical capital-intensive OEM (owner-FCF DCF + adaptations) and a captive lender, Ford Credit, which runs 9.6:1 financial-statement leverage, funds a $146B receivables book with $139B of its own debt, and cannot be run through an owner-FCF engine (its 'debt' is operating funding and its OCF swings with receivables, not with earnings). Per SKILL.md the parts are valued separately and summed: (1) an owner-FCF DCF on 'Company excluding Ford Credit' (Ford Blue + Model e + Pro + Corporate Other, Ford's own supplemental consolidating basis, F_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:5246-5312), and (2) Ford Credit added to the equity bridge at book equity. NET DEBT is AUTOMOTIVE ONLY, as the financial-parser intended: Company-excl-Ford-Credit debt $23,689M (4,154 current + 19,535 long-term, incl. the ~$3.8B DOE loan assumed in the BlueOval SK unwind) less unrestricted cash $14,024M and marketable securities $11,064M = net cash $1,399M at 2026-09-30. Consolidated total_debt of $163B is NOT used; $139,393M of it is Ford Credit funding and is already netted inside Ford Credit's $14,537M book equity. FORD CREDIT at 1.0x book ($14,537M = sector assets 160,807 - liabilities 146,270). Justification: FY2026 EBT guided ~$2.8B, ~$2.2B after tax, ROE ~15% against an 11% cost of equity for a wholesale-funded captive with a rising loss-to-receivables ratio (67bps Q3-26 vs 62bps) and softening residuals -- a justified P/B of 1.0-1.4x; 1.0x is the conservative end and is scenario-independent in the bridge (bull would support ~1.3x, a severe credit cycle ~0.7x; +/-$1.00/share). MATCHING-ASSET RULE: because Ford Credit's equity is in the bridge, its EBT and its distributions to the parent ($1.65B FY2025, $2.6B 9M-2026) are EXCLUDED from the flows; the industrial EBIT path starts from Company adjusted EBIT excluding Ford Credit EBT. Likewise automotive interest income (~$1.0B/yr, Company-excl-Ford-Credit share of the $1,490M consolidated investment-related interest income, F_Annual_FY2025.txt:8320) is stripped from EBIT because the cash earning it is in the bridge. PENSION/OPEB: net liability $4.6B at FY2025 ($0.2B pension net underfunding + $4.4B unfunded pay-as-you-go OPEB, F_Annual_FY2025.txt:6635-6641) is debt-like and deducted in the bridge tax-effected at 21% (-$3,634M); service cost remains inside EBIT. FY0 = FY2026E: 9M-2026 actuals plus a Q4 estimate (revenue ex-Credit 130,792 + ~44,700 = 175,500; adj EBIT ex-Credit 6.3B 9M + ~1.65B Q4 = 7.95B, the midpoint of the raised 10.5-11.0B guidance less ~2.8B Ford Credit EBT; D&A ex-Credit 3,564 9M -> ~4.8B; capex 7.0B 9M -> ~10.0B guided). The balance sheet is the Q3 one, so Q4-2026 cash generation (~$1-2B of adjusted FCF) is not credited anywhere -- a small conservatism. ENGINE EBITDA DEFINITION: Ford's adjusted EBIT already expenses SBC, so ebitda_margin_path = (adj EBIT ex-Credit ex-interest-income + D&A + SBC) / revenue ex-Credit; history on that basis is 8.0% FY2023, 7.3% FY2024, 4.8% FY2025 (Novelis fire, tariffs), ~6.9% FY2026E. The paths are stated NET of a recurring special-item cash charge (restructuring, EV program cancellation payments of up to $4B still to come, field-service actions): 0.5pp of revenue in 2027-28 and 0.3pp thereafter -- Ford has booked 'special' cash costs every year for a decade. FORD'S OWN 'ALL OTHER AND TIMING DIFFERENCES' (+$3.6-5.2B/yr in its adjusted-FCF bridge, largely warranty accruals running ahead of warranty cash while the liability grew $14.0B -> $17.7B) is given NO credit: the model assumes cash warranty cost equals the expense. That, plus moving Ford Credit distributions and interest income to the bridge and deducting restructuring/pension cash, is why the industrial owner FCF (~$0.7B FY2026E, ~$0.2B Y1) sits far below Ford's $6.0-7.0B adjusted FCF guidance; reported_fcf here is Company adjusted FCF guidance midpoint $6.5B less ~$3.3B Ford Credit distributions = $3.2B, and last_fcf = 3,200 - 430 SBC - 1,000 interest income = 1,770 (still pre-restructuring and pre-pension-contribution, ~$1.8B/yr, which the component build absorbs via the special-item haircut and the capex/margin paths). WORKING CAPITAL: Ford's industrial working capital is structurally negative (payables $27.0B > receivables $8.6B + inventory $16.2B) so growth releases cash, but at 1-2% growth the effect is <0.1% of revenue; wc_capture set to 0. CASH TAX: $22B of deferred tax assets ex-Credit (NOLs, credits) keep cash taxes far below the 20% adjusted book rate (cash taxes ~$0.5-1.0B/yr on ~$7-8B of industrial EBIT in 2023-25); the path ramps 12% -> 21% over six years. SANITY-CHECK WARNING for the orchestrator: any EV/EBITDA multiple computed from consolidated total_debt ($163B) will be meaningless for Ford; use AutomotiveDebt or compare on P/E and P/B.

equity_bridge.item: Ford Credit at 1.0x book equity (sector assets 160,807 - liabilities 146,270 at 2026-09-30)
equity_bridge.note: F_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:5301,5312; Ford Credit EBT and distributions are excluded from the flows (matching-asset rule). 9.6:1 leverage, FY2026 EBT guided ~$2.8B.

equity_bridge.item: Net pension and OPEB liability, tax-effected at 21% (4,600 x 0.79)
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 10-K: pension net underfunded $0.2B, OPEB unfunded $4.4B, pay-as-you-go from Company cash (F_Annual_FY2025.txt:6635-6641). Debt-like; service cost stays in EBIT.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle nominal revenue growth for a mature OEM (volume flat-to-down, pricing +1-2%); no historical CAGR is usable as a forward proxy
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR is -5.9% (FY2022 $43.2B -> FY2025 $36.0B after $17.4B of FY2025 special items) against revenue +5.8%: book value is being destroyed by EV impairments while revenue grows -- flag. EPS CAGRs are undefined (FY2025 GAAP EPS -$2.06; adjusted EPS fell 1.88 -> 1.09 over FY2022-25). FCF CAGR is on Company adjusted FCF ($9.1B FY2022 -> $3.5B FY2025); consolidated reported FCF is dominated by Ford Credit receivables swings and is not a usable series.
historical_growth.notes: Consolidated revenue FY2020 127,144 / FY2022 158,057 / FY2025 187,267. Revenue ex-Ford Credit 165,901 / 172,706 / 173,996 for FY2023-25 (F_Annual_FY2025.txt:7634). Company adjusted EBIT ex-Ford Credit 9.1 / 8.6 / 4.2B FY2023-25, 6.3B 9M-2026. Owner-FCF CAGRs on the consolidated series are not meaningful for a company with an embedded lender; see valuation_philosophy for the mid-cycle framing used instead.

base.narrative: Mid-cycle recovery with Model e losses roughly halving by 2029-30. Engine EBITDA 6.7% in 2027 (7.2% underlying less 0.5pp special-item cash) vs ~6.9% FY2026E, rising to 8.1% by 2031 (EBIT ex-Credit ex-interest ~4.6%, a little above the 2023-24 level of ~4.3-4.5%). Capex stays at the guided ~$10B through 2028 (Universal EV platform, Louisville, Ford Energy) then normalises to 5.0% of revenue; D&A rises toward 3.2% as the post-impairment asset base rebuilds. Cash tax ramps 12% -> 21% as DTAs are consumed.

bull.narrative: Model e reaches breakeven by 2029 on the Universal EV platform, Ford Pro holds ~$7B EBIT and grows software/services attach, tariff refunds and Novelis normalisation land, no US recession in the window. Engine EBITDA reaches 9.5% (EBIT ex-Credit ex-interest ~6.1%, roughly Ford's long-stated 8% total-company ambition net of Credit). Capex falls to 4.8% of revenue as the EV build-out completes.

bear.narrative: A 2028 US auto downturn (SAAR ~14.5M, revenue -6%) with Ford's largely fixed cost base: engine EBITDA troughs at 5.0% (near the FY2025 Novelis/tariff year of 4.8%), Model e losses persist near $3-4B as the EV pivot slips, 50% Canadian steel/auto tariffs from 2027 bite, recall/warranty cash catches up with the $17.7B accrual. Recovery only to 6.8% (EBIT ex-Credit ex-interest ~3.3%), below the 2023-24 level, with capex unable to fall below 5.0% because the hybrid/EREV and Universal EV programmes must still be funded. Terminal cap 10x. Note the bridge still carries Ford Credit at 1.0x book; a genuine credit cycle would take that below book, so this bear is not the worst case.

scenario_narratives.base: Ford Blue and Ford Pro remain a ~$12-13B EBIT franchise built on F-Series, Super Duty and Transit; Model e's loss narrows from ~$4B toward ~$1.5-2B by 2030 as the Universal EV platform and the hybrid/EREV tilt replace the cancelled Lightning-era programmes; Ford Credit earns ~15% on ~$14.5B of equity and is worth about book. The industrial business generates thin owner FCF ($0.2B 2027 rising to ~$3.5B by 2031) because capex stays near $10B while D&A is ~$5B and warranty/restructuring cash is charged in full. Value is therefore roughly half bridge (Ford Credit + automotive net cash - pension/OPEB) and half a mid-cycle terminal value capped at 12x.
scenario_narratives.bull: Everything management has guided to actually happens: Model e breaks even by 2029 on a sub-$30k EV pickup, Ford Pro's software and services attach lifts its margin, the tariff receivable is refunded and no new tariffs arrive, Novelis costs roll off, US SAAR holds 16-17M for a decade. Engine EBITDA reaches 9.5% of revenue and capex falls to 4.8%, giving owner FCF of ~$6-7B by the terminal year. Ford Credit would also be worth more than book in this world, which the fixed bridge does not credit.
scenario_narratives.bear: A 2028 recession hits an OEM with UAW-level fixed costs, Model e keeps losing $3-4B a year as EV adoption stalls without the $7,500 credit, 50% Canadian tariffs land in 2027, and the record recall run becomes cash as the $17.7B warranty liability unwinds. Industrial owner FCF is negative through 2029 and recovers only to ~$1.5B; the stock is worth little more than its bridge (Ford Credit book, net cash, less OPEB).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: the thesis rests on an unproven EV pivot (a $19.5B impairment one year ago shows the prior plan failed), tariff policy is an explicit exclusion from management's own guidance, recall costs have set records two years running, and a US auto downturn inside a 10-year window is the historical norm, not a tail. Bull cut from 35% to 20%: it needs Model e breakeven, Pro margin expansion, tariff relief and no recession to all hold at once. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Sum-of-parts owner-FCF valuation. The automotive business (Company excluding Ford Credit) is valued on a 10-year component build of unlevered owner FCF -- Ford's adjusted EBIT ex-Credit, stripped of interest income, net of a recurring special-item cash charge, with capex and D&A modelled separately and cash taxes ramping to statutory -- discounted at a single 9.5% USD WACC with a 12x terminal cap (10x bear). Automotive net debt uses AutomotiveDebt ($23.7B) against automotive cash and securities ($25.1B), never the $163B consolidated figure. Ford Credit enters the bridge at 1.0x book equity ($14.5B) and its EBT and distributions leave the flows. The $4.6B net pension/OPEB liability is deducted tax-effected. Ford's own 'timing differences' (+$3.6-5.2B/yr) are given no credit, so the model's industrial FCF is deliberately far below Ford's adjusted FCF guidance; the gap is mostly warranty accruals the model assumes will be paid.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value is ~half of automotive EV in base and is set by a single mid-cycle margin assumption (8.1% engine EBITDA); every 1pp is roughly $3-4/share
Ford Credit at 1.0x book is scenario-independent; a credit cycle (loss-to-receivables already 67bps vs 14bps in 2022) or residual-value shock would take it below book, ~-$1/share per 0.3x
Tariffs: management guidance excludes any new action; a 50% Canadian steel/auto tariff from Jan-2027 is flagged but not in guidance
Model e: losses guided at ~$4B for FY2026 with breakeven 'around 2029'; up to $4B of further cash cancellation costs are disclosed as possible
Warranty/recall: the $17.7B liability is assumed to convert to cash at the accrual rate; a faster unwind would push owner FCF negative for several years
The Q3-2026 balance sheet omits Q4-2026 cash generation (~$1-2B); the next update should roll the anchors to the FY2026 10-K
